pal-picard.title: Divisors, line bundles, and the Picard group

questions.q: Let $D$ be a divisor on a smooth projective variety $X$. Which set is $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(D))$?
choices: the group of all rational functions on $X$
questions.explain: The line bundle $\mathcal{O}(D)$ has global sections equal to rational functions whose pole order at each component of $D$ is bounded above by the multiplicity of $D$ there — equivalently, $\mathrm{div}(f) + D \ge 0$. The zero function is included by convention.
$\mathrm{Pic}(\mathbb{P}^n) = \mathbb{Z}$, generated by the hyperplane class $\mathcal{O}(1)$. Every line bundle is $\mathcal{O}(d)$ for a unique $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ (the degree).
$\binom{3+2}{2} = \binom{5}{2} = 10$. Equivalently, the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree $3$ in $3$ variables has dimension $10$.

pal-very-ample.title: Very ample, ample, and Serre's theorem

questions.q: Which of the following is the cleanest definition of $L$ being very ample on a projective variety $X$?
choices: Every irreducible curve $C \subset X$ satisfies $L \cdot C > 0$.
$L^{\otimes n}$ is generated by global sections for every $n \ge 1$.
The complete linear system $|L|$ defines a closed embedding $X \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}(H^0(X, L)^\vee)$.
$\chi(X, L^{\otimes n})$ is a polynomial in $n$ of degree $\dim X$.
questions.explain: Very ampleness is the embedding property: the sections of $L$ separate points and tangent vectors and yield a closed immersion into projective space. Choice (a) is the nef condition (and not even sufficient); (b) is base-point-freeness; (d) is true but applies to every line bundle on a projective variety (Hilbert polynomial).

questions.q: Serre's theorem says $L$ is ample on a projective $X$ iff:
choices: for every coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ there is $n_0$ with $H^i(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes L^{\otimes n}) = 0$ for all $i > 0$ and $n \ge n_0$
questions.explain: Serre's vanishing/ampleness theorem: ampleness is equivalent to eventual vanishing of all higher cohomology after twisting any coherent sheaf by enough copies of $L$. Choice (c) is necessary but not sufficient (need the full Nakai criterion); (a) and (d) are far weaker.

questions.q: Which is true of the relationship between very ample and ample?
choices: Every ample line bundle is very ample.
$L$ ample iff $L^{\otimes n}$ is very ample for some $n \ge 1$.
Very ample line bundles need not be ample.
Ampleness is a property of $\mathcal{O}_X$, not of $L$.
questions.explain: Ampleness is the property that some tensor power is very ample. The simplest counterexample to (a) is a degree-$1$ line bundle $L$ on an elliptic curve $E$: it is ample (positive degree) but not very ample. By Riemann–Roch $h^0(L) = 1$ in degree $1$, so there are not even enough sections to define a map; only at degree $\ge 3$ does $|L|$ embed $E$.

questions.q: The Nakai–Moishezon criterion states $L$ is ample on a projective $X$ iff:
choices: $L \cdot C > 0$ for every irreducible curve $C \subset X$
$L^{\dim Y} \cdot Y > 0$ for every irreducible subvariety $Y \subseteq X$ of positive dimension
questions.explain: Nakai–Moishezon: ampleness is detected by positive top self-intersection on every positive-dimensional subvariety, including $X$ itself. Choice (a) — positivity on curves alone — is exactly the nef condition, which is strictly weaker than ample.

questions.q: On $\mathbb{P}^2$, the hyperplane class $H$ satisfies $H^2 = 1$. By Nakai, $\mathcal{O}(d)$ is ample iff $d > 0$. What is the smallest positive integer $d$ such that $\mathcal{O}(d)$ is very ample on $\mathbb{P}^2$?
questions.explain: $\mathcal{O}(1)$ is already very ample: its sections give the identity embedding $\mathbb{P}^2 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^2$. For $\mathbb{P}^n$, very ampleness and ampleness coincide for every positive twist.

questions.q: Why does the ample cone live in $N^1(X)_\mathbb{R} = \mathrm{Pic}(X)/\equiv \,\otimes\, \mathbb{R}$ (numerical equivalence) rather than in $\mathrm{Pic}(X)_\mathbb{R}$ directly?
choices: Numerical equivalence is finer than algebraic equivalence.
Ampleness is a numerical condition: it depends only on intersection numbers, so passes to the quotient by numerical equivalence.
$\mathrm{Pic}(X)$ may be infinite-dimensional, but $N^1(X)$ is finite rank.
questions.explain: Both reasons matter. Ampleness depends only on numerical data (intersection products), so factors through $N^1(X)$; and the Néron–Severi theorem ensures $N^1(X)$ has finite rank, making convex-geometry questions about the ample cone tractable.

pal-nef-big.title: Nef, big, and the cone of curves

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct relation between the ample and nef cones in $N^1(X)_\mathbb{R}$?
choices: $\mathrm{Nef}(X)$ is the topological closure of $\mathrm{Amp}(X)$, and $\mathrm{Amp}(X)$ is its interior
questions.explain: Kleiman's theorem: $\mathrm{Nef}(X) = \overline{\mathrm{Amp}(X)}$ and $\mathrm{Amp}(X) = \mathrm{int}\,\mathrm{Nef}(X)$. Both cones are convex. The two coincide on $\mathbb{P}^n$ but on a blown-up surface they differ — the exceptional curve has zero intersection with itself's contraction class.

questions.q: Kleiman duality says $\mathrm{Nef}(X)$ is dual to which cone?
choices: the effective cone $\mathrm{Eff}(X)$ of effective divisor classes
the closed cone of curves $\overline{NE}(X) \subset N_1(X)_\mathbb{R}$
questions.explain: Kleiman: $L \in \mathrm{Nef}(X) \iff L \cdot \alpha \ge 0$ for all $\alpha \in \overline{NE}(X)$. So $\mathrm{Nef}(X)$ is exactly the dual cone of the Mori cone $\overline{NE}(X)$ inside the perfect pairing $N^1(X)_\mathbb{R} \times N_1(X)_\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$.

questions.q: Which of the following is the cleanest definition of a big divisor $D$ on a projective variety of dimension $n$?
choices: $h^0(X, \mathcal{O}(mD)) \ge c \, m^n$ for some $c > 0$ and all $m \gg 0$
$D$ is an effective sum of irreducible divisors
questions.explain: Bigness is the maximal-growth condition on global sections — sections grow at the top dimension rate $m^n$. Equivalently, $D = A + E$ with $A$ ample and $E$ effective (Kodaira's lemma). Ample $\Rightarrow$ big, but bigness is strictly weaker.

questions.q: Kodaira's embedding theorem characterizes projective compact Kähler manifolds. The criterion is:
choices: $X$ admits a positive line bundle (a Hermitian line bundle whose curvature is a Kähler form)
$X$ has a non-trivial holomorphic vector field
$X$ is a complete intersection in some $\mathbb{P}^N$
questions.explain: Kodaira (1954): $X$ projective $\iff$ $X$ has a positive line bundle. Curvature positivity (a metric notion) and ampleness (an algebraic notion) coincide for line bundles on projective manifolds — this is the bridge between complex differential geometry and algebraic geometry.

questions.q: Given a positive line bundle $L$ on a compact Kähler $X$, the Kodaira map for $n \gg 0$ is:
choices: $X \to H^0(X, L^{\otimes n})$ given by evaluation
questions.explain: The Kodaira map sends $x \in X$ to the hyperplane in $H^0(X, L^{\otimes n})$ consisting of sections vanishing at $x$, i.e. a point of the dual projective space. For $n$ large enough that $L^{\otimes n}$ is very ample, this map is a closed embedding.

choices: exactly those whose lattice $\Lambda$ admits a Riemann form (a Hodge metric) — these are abelian varieties
none, since complex tori are never projective
questions.explain: By Kodaira, a complex torus is projective iff it admits a positive line bundle. The existence of such a line bundle is equivalent to the existence of a Riemann form on $\Lambda$ — a positive-definite Hermitian form whose imaginary part takes integer values on $\Lambda \times \Lambda$. Projective tori are abelian varieties, and for $g \ge 2$ a generic complex torus has no Riemann form.

questions.q: Let $L$ be ample on a smooth projective $X/\mathbb{C}$ of dimension $n$, and $K_X$ the canonical bundle. Kodaira vanishing says:
questions.explain: Kodaira: $H^i(X, K_X \otimes L) = 0$ for $i > 0$ when $L$ is ample. The factor of $K_X$ is essential — without it, the conclusion can fail even for line bundles that are positive in a weaker sense (on an elliptic curve $E$, the trivial bundle $\mathcal{O}_E$ is nef but $H^1(E, \mathcal{O}_E) \cong \mathbb{C} \ne 0$).

questions.q: Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing extends Kodaira to which class of line bundles?
choices: $L$ such that $L \equiv$ (nef and big) — possibly with simple-normal-crossing fractional boundary
questions.explain: Kawamata–Viehweg: if $L$ is nef and big (and the relevant pair has at worst klt singularities), then $H^i(X, K_X \otimes L) = 0$ for $i > 0$. The flexibility to allow nef-big rather than ample is exactly what powers the minimal model program: contracted divisors only stay nef, not ample.

questions.q: Let $L = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n}(d)$ with $d \ge 1$. By Kodaira (or direct computation), how many $i > 0$ satisfy $H^i(\mathbb{P}^n, K_{\mathbb{P}^n} \otimes L) \ne 0$?
questions.explain: $\mathcal{O}(d)$ is ample on $\mathbb{P}^n$ for $d \ge 1$, so Kodaira vanishing applies and gives $H^i(\mathbb{P}^n, K_{\mathbb{P}^n} \otimes \mathcal{O}(d)) = 0$ for all $i > 0$. (Concretely $K_{\mathbb{P}^n} = \mathcal{O}(-n-1)$, so the bundle is $\mathcal{O}(d - n - 1)$; one checks higher cohomology vanishes for $d \ge 1$.)
